_about: Long-form UI design content for /flow-design (brief mode), flow-planner, flow-plan-checker 2c, flow-executor, the flow-reviewer design lens and flow-verifier. Brand values never live here: the brand base is the project's own source (DESIGN.md `brand:`, config.json design.brand). template_tells are generic and brand-neutral.
template_tells: slate/zinc/neutral/gray UI chrome with a single blue, indigo or violet accent and no other color role
Inter, Geist or system-ui for every element at one or two weights, with no display or contrasting face
flat type scale: page title under 2x body size, so nothing reads first
rounded-lg/xl cards with a soft shadow and a 1px gray border on every surface, cards nested in cards
a 3- or 4-up row of identical stat cards (label, big number, small % delta) at the top of every dashboard
centered hero with gradient text, blurred gradient blobs, or a glassmorphism panel
purple-to-blue (or pink-to-violet) gradients on buttons, headings or backgrounds
a lucide icon in every card header, nav item and empty state, all the same size and stroke
identical shell: fixed left sidebar of icon+label links plus a top bar with search and an avatar
default shadcn/ui Button, Badge, Card, Table and Input styling unchanged (default radius, ring, muted-foreground text)
uniform 16px/24px spacing everywhere, same gap inside and between groups, so there is no grouping or hierarchy
every section centered in a max-w container with equal margins, nothing anchored to a left edge or grid
emoji used as icons or section markers
pill badges in pastel green/yellow/red for every status, regardless of importance
placeholder copy and data: 'Welcome back', lorem ipsum, round fake metrics (+12.5%), generic avatars
brief_prompts: Brand base: where is the canonical brand source (shared tokens package, brand repo dir, or Claude Design project URL), and which version or date? If none is known, say so: it is flagged, never invented.
Siblings: which other apps share this brand base (name + DESIGN.md path or a screenshot when known)?
Distinct: in one line each, what makes this app look different from each sibling (accent within the base's allowed roles, layout, density, hero/dashboard composition)?
Users: who uses it, how often, for how long per session, and on what screen (laptop, wall monitor, phone, field tablet)?
Environment: lighting, attention level and task (glance at status, scan a table all day, fill a form once a quarter)?
Density: how much must be on one screen at once (rows visible, fields per form, charts per view)?
Personality: three traits, each stated as a visual fact per references/impact.md (e.g. 'tight 28px table rows', 'one saturated accent used only for the primary action'), not adjectives.
Reference direction: a named era, style or product it should resemble (e.g. Swiss International, Bloomberg terminal, Linear, a printed timetable), never 'modern' or 'clean'.
Not this: what must it not look like, from template_tells and from any sibling it could be confused with?
